scope: Educational comparisons only; diet-ranking catalogue remains unchanged.

variants.geneRole: Helps produce a folate form used to recycle homocysteine to methionine.
variants.variantMeaning: The common 677C>T protein change is written G>A on the genomic forward strand. A corresponds to 677T.
variants.evidence: Functional and biomarker evidence; nutritional outcome depends on folate status.

comparisons.GG: No A (677T) copies at this marker. Does not guarantee normal folate or homocysteine.
comparisons.AG: One A (677T) copy; average enzyme/biomarker effects are generally less pronounced than AA.
comparisons.AA: Two A (677T) copies; lower average enzyme activity and greater susceptibility to higher homocysteine, especially with low folate.

variants.dietMeaning: Review actual folate, B12 and homocysteine measurements when clinically indicated; this marker does not choose a supplement form or dose.
variants.limitations: Common variation is not severe MTHFR deficiency. Food folate and folic acid can still be used; no fixed personal enzyme-activity percentage is inferred.

variants.geneRole: Supports folate-dependent homocysteine recycling.
variants.variantMeaning: A1298C changes a protein residue in the regulatory region. Forward G corresponds to gene-oriented 1298C; T corresponds to 1298A.
variants.evidence: Functional evidence; isolated biomarker effects are less consistent than for rs1801133.

comparisons.TT: No G (1298C) copies. This does not describe the separate 677 marker.
comparisons.GT: One G (1298C) copy. This alone does not establish high homocysteine or folate deficiency.
comparisons.GG: Two G (1298C) copies; reduced activity has been observed experimentally, but a personal nutrient requirement cannot be calculated.

variants.dietMeaning: Review actual folate, B12 and homocysteine measurements when clinically indicated; this marker does not choose a supplement form or dose.
variants.limitations: The combined effect with rs1801133 requires careful interpretation; Bloom does not infer phase or a combined activity score.

variants.geneRole: Helps reactivate the B12-dependent methionine synthase enzyme.
variants.variantMeaning: The common A66G variant changes Ile22 to Met. It has been studied in one-carbon metabolism.
variants.evidence: Candidate-variant/biomarker evidence; no established genotype-specific nutrient target.

comparisons.AA: Ile/Ile at the commonly described protein change.
comparisons.AG: Ile/Met: one copy of each allele. This does not demonstrate impaired B12 recycling.
comparisons.GG: Met/Met. Published biomarker associations do not justify automatically classifying this as deficient or impaired.

variants.dietMeaning: Review actual folate, B12 and homocysteine measurements when clinically indicated; this marker does not choose a supplement form or dose.
variants.limitations: Enzyme-pathway involvement is different from evidence that extra B12 or methylated supplements improve outcomes for this genotype.

variants.geneRole: Encodes the B12-dependent enzyme that converts homocysteine to methionine.
variants.variantMeaning: A2756G changes Asp919 to Gly. The marker is studied in folate/B12-related metabolism.
variants.evidence: Candidate-variant associations; personal functional direction remains uncertain.

comparisons.AA: Asp/Asp at this marker. Does not rule out B12 or folate problems.
comparisons.AG: Asp/Gly. No reliable intermediate nutrient requirement has been established.
comparisons.GG: Gly/Gly. Biomarker effects are not sufficiently consistent to infer a deficiency or prescribe a supplement.

variants.dietMeaning: Review actual folate, B12 and homocysteine measurements when clinically indicated; this marker does not choose a supplement form or dose.
variants.limitations: Do not interpret a common MTR call as a diagnosis of rare methionine-synthase deficiency.

variants.geneRole: Helps move homocysteine into the transsulfuration pathway toward cysteine; the enzyme uses vitamin B6.
variants.variantMeaning: C699T is a synonymous marker: it does not change the encoded amino acid. Forward A corresponds to the gene-oriented T allele.
variants.evidence: Inconsistent candidate-gene findings; insufficient evidence for a useful dietary activity ranking.

comparisons.GG: No A copies at this synonymous marker; not a measurement of CBS activity.
comparisons.AG: One A copy; not evidence of an overactive CBS enzyme or excess sulfur/ammonia.
comparisons.AA: Two A copies; does not establish an overactive pathway or a need to restrict sulfur foods.

variants.dietMeaning: This SNP does not justify restricting protein, sulfur-containing vegetables or B6 on its own.
variants.limitations: Studies of homocysteine have not consistently supported the claimed functional effect; rare disease-causing CBS variants are a separate issue.

variants.geneRole: Controls whether certain blood-group-related sugars are displayed in secretions and on gut surfaces, influencing the microbial habitat.
variants.variantMeaning: The A stop allele can disable FUT2 secretor function. This marker explains a common non-secretor form in some populations.
variants.evidence: Established secretor biology; B12 associations do not directly measure usable B12.

comparisons.GG: Two G copies: compatible with secretor status at this marker.
comparisons.AG: One G copy generally preserves secretor function; this is not a halfway non-secretor state.
comparisons.AA: Two A copies: compatible with non-secretor status from this common stop variant.

variants.dietMeaning: Use actual B12 status and symptoms. Do not select a probiotic, infer a bacterial deficiency or assume poor B12 absorption from this marker.
variants.limitations: Other FUT2 variants and ancestry matter. Higher total B12 can reflect binding-protein differences rather than better cellular B12 supply.

variants.geneRole: Participates in desaturation steps that help form longer-chain polyunsaturated fats.
variants.variantMeaning: A common FADS-cluster marker associated with fatty-acid composition and inferred desaturase activity. It is distinct from rs174550.
variants.evidence: Replicated fatty-acid associations; causal variants and dietary response vary by population.

comparisons.TT: No C copies at this marker; the comparison group in several desaturase studies.
comparisons.CT: One C copy; population-average fatty-acid profiles can differ from TT and CC.
comparisons.CC: Two C copies; associated with lower inferred desaturase activity in some studied groups, not a measured personal conversion rate.

variants.dietMeaning: Consider the overall fat pattern and relevant measurements; this is not a calculated fish-oil requirement or a mandate to eat seafood.
variants.limitations: Lipid ratios are proxies for activity. Do not extrapolate an exact ALA-to-EPA/DHA conversion percentage.

variants.geneRole: Participates in desaturation steps that help form longer-chain polyunsaturated fats.
variants.variantMeaning: An intronic FADS1 marker investigated in diet trials comparing TT and CC groups.
variants.evidence: Human dietary intervention and mechanistic evidence; CT is not directly characterized by every trial.

comparisons.TT: Associated with higher inferred desaturase activity than CC in the cited research.
comparisons.CT: One C and one T copy. A precisely intermediate response is not established by trials enrolling only TT and CC.
comparisons.CC: Associated with lower inferred activity than TT in the cited research; actual lipid responses depend on dietary inputs.

variants.dietMeaning: Consider the overall fat pattern and relevant measurements; this is not a calculated fish-oil requirement or a mandate to eat seafood.
variants.limitations: The cited trial contrasted homozygotes. No per-genotype oil dose or assured health benefit follows from those findings.

variants.geneRole: Converts beta-carotene from plant foods into a vitamin A precursor.
variants.variantMeaning: The R267S protein variant has been studied alongside other BCO1 variants in beta-carotene conversion.
variants.evidence: Small human functional studies; combined variants and food context matter.

comparisons.AA: No T copies at this marker. This alone does not guarantee efficient vitamin A conversion.
comparisons.AT: One T copy; a precise reduction in personal conversion is not established from this SNP alone.
comparisons.TT: Two T copies; research implicates the variant in conversion variability, especially in combinations with other BCO1 variants.

variants.dietMeaning: Assess vitamin A intake from both carotenoid and preformed sources. Do not calculate a retinol dose from this SNP.
variants.limitations: Large conversion percentages reported for combined variants must not be assigned to rs12934922 alone; this call does not diagnose vitamin A deficiency.

variants.geneRole: Helps convert vitamin D into circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D.
variants.variantMeaning: A common regulatory-region marker associated with the blood vitamin D biomarker.
variants.evidence: Large human GWAS; individual supplement response is not determined by the marker.

comparisons.AA: No G copies; associated with relatively higher average 25-hydroxyvitamin D than G-carrying groups in cited studies.
comparisons.AG: One G copy; a modest population-level tendency toward lower biomarker levels.
comparisons.GG: Two G copies; associated with lower average levels, without establishing a personal deficiency.

variants.dietMeaning: Measured 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intake and clinical context guide any supplementation.
variants.limitations: Season, sun exposure, body composition and other genes can outweigh the contribution of this marker.

variants.geneRole: Converts 25-hydroxyvitamin D to the active hormone calcitriol.
variants.variantMeaning: A promoter-region marker, often written -1260C>A in gene-oriented notation; forward alleles are G/T.
variants.evidence: Candidate-variant and functional-context evidence; dietary actionability is limited.

comparisons.GG: Two G copies at this promoter marker. Bloom does not assign a vitamin D activation rate.
comparisons.GT: One G and one T copy. No validated intermediate activation or dose requirement is available.
comparisons.TT: Two T copies. No reliable personal active-vitamin-D prediction is calculated.

variants.dietMeaning: Interpret vitamin D measurements in clinical context rather than treating the genotype as a reason to take active vitamin D.
variants.limitations: Candidate studies do not establish a general-population genotype-specific dose or a simple universal best genotype.

variants.geneRole: Helps regulate iron absorption through iron-sensing and hepcidin signalling.
variants.variantMeaning: The A allele encodes C282Y, an important hereditary-haemochromatosis variant.
variants.evidence: Established clinical relevance; penetrance is incomplete and context dependent.

comparisons.GG: No C282Y A copies. Other causes of iron overload or deficiency remain possible.
comparisons.AG: One C282Y copy. This usually differs substantially from having two copies; other HFE variants and iron studies matter.
comparisons.AA: Two C282Y copies. This warrants clinical confirmation and assessment of iron status; it is not proof of iron-overload disease.

variants.dietMeaning: Ferritin, transferrin saturation and clinical assessment guide decisions. A consumer call does not authorize iron treatment or a restrictive diet.
variants.limitations: Sex, age, ancestry, other variants and environmental factors affect expression. No diagnosis or penetrance percentage is assigned to the individual.

variants.geneRole: Participates in regulation of iron absorption.
variants.variantMeaning: The G allele encodes H63D. Its clinical significance differs from the separate C282Y variant.
variants.evidence: Established variant identity; standalone clinical effects are smaller and context dependent.

comparisons.CC: No H63D G copies at this marker.
comparisons.CG: One H63D copy; by itself this does not establish iron overload.
comparisons.GG: Two H63D copies; clinical expression is generally less penetrant than C282Y homozygosity and needs actual iron studies.

variants.dietMeaning: Use ferritin and transferrin saturation; interpret alongside C282Y and medical history.
variants.limitations: One H63D and one C282Y result does not establish which chromosome each is on. No compound-haplotype diagnosis is inferred.

variants.geneRole: Encodes matriptase-2, which regulates hepcidin and therefore iron availability.
variants.variantMeaning: A common protein-changing marker associated with iron and haemoglobin traits.
variants.evidence: Replicated biomarker associations and a human iron-absorption study.

comparisons.GG: No A copies; relatively higher iron-related biomarkers in the cited population comparison.
comparisons.AG: One A copy; associated with modestly lower average iron-related biomarkers than GG.
comparisons.AA: Two A copies; associated with a larger average reduction than AG in some studies, without diagnosing deficiency.

variants.dietMeaning: Check measured haemoglobin and iron studies when indicated; do not automatically start iron supplements.
variants.limitations: Effects vary by ancestry and physiological context. This common variant is different from rare causes of iron-refractory anaemia.

variants.geneRole: Influences pathways involved in pancreatic insulin secretion and glucose regulation.
variants.variantMeaning: A common regulatory marker associated with type 2 diabetes susceptibility.
variants.evidence: Strong human genetic association; genotype-specific food prescriptions are unproven.

comparisons.CC: No T copies at the commonly studied C/T marker. This does not rule out diabetes.
comparisons.CT: One T copy; associated with greater susceptibility than CC on average.
comparisons.TT: Two T copies; generally a stronger population association than CT, not a diagnosis or a personal probability.

variants.dietMeaning: Prioritize measured glucose, HbA1c and the overall eating pattern rather than a genotype-derived carbohydrate limit.
variants.limitations: The table covers the studied C/T pair. Other reported alleles are held for review rather than silently translated.

variants.geneRole: Encodes a melatonin receptor involved in circadian signalling and pancreatic insulin release.
variants.variantMeaning: The G allele at this intronic marker is associated with higher fasting glucose and a weaker early insulin response.
variants.evidence: Replicated human GWAS and insulin-secretion studies.

comparisons.CC: No G copies; comparison group with lower average fasting glucose in cited cohorts.
comparisons.CG: One G copy; associated with a modest shift toward higher fasting glucose.
comparisons.GG: Two G copies; a stronger average association, not a diagnosis or an assured meal response.

variants.dietMeaning: Use actual glucose measures and sleep/meal context. Do not set a rigid eating cutoff or start/stop melatonin solely from this SNP.
variants.limitations: A population-average association does not determine an individual response to a particular meal or melatonin dose.

variants.geneRole: Encodes a transporter involved in intestinal vitamin C uptake and kidney reabsorption.
variants.variantMeaning: A protein-changing marker associated with circulating vitamin C; the studied forward T allele is the vitamin-C-lowering allele.
variants.evidence: Replicated human biomarker association; clinical supplement benefit is not established.

comparisons.CC: No T copies at this marker. Vitamin C status still depends on intake and other factors.
comparisons.CT: One T copy; associated with lower average circulating vitamin C than CC.
comparisons.TT: Two T copies; a rare group for which individual precision is limited. No personal deficiency is inferred.

variants.dietMeaning: Review fruit/vegetable intake and clinical context rather than assigning high-dose vitamin C from a genotype.
variants.limitations: A biomarker association does not establish that increasing a supplement dose improves health outcomes.

sources.title: Vitamin C association in five studies

variants.geneRole: Marks a region involved in the biology of appetite and body-weight regulation.
variants.variantMeaning: An intronic association marker. It tags a larger regulatory region rather than providing a direct calorie-burn measurement.
variants.evidence: Replicated obesity association; appetite findings and effect size depend on context.

comparisons.TT: No A copies at this marker. This does not protect against weight gain.
comparisons.AT: One A copy; associated with higher average adiposity susceptibility than TT.
comparisons.AA: Two A copies; generally a stronger association than AT, without determining body weight or metabolism.

variants.dietMeaning: Practical satiety and eating habits may be relevant for everyone; do not derive a calorie target or claim a slow metabolism from this SNP.
variants.limitations: The marker does not explain all appetite differences and is not a test of willpower. Associations are not destiny.

variants.geneRole: Lies near a gene central to brain pathways regulating appetite and energy balance.
variants.variantMeaning: A common noncoding marker near MC4R, not a diagnosis of a rare MC4R loss-of-function disorder.
variants.evidence: Replicated human body-weight association.

comparisons.TT: No C copies; lower average susceptibility than C-carrying groups in the cited association.
comparisons.CT: One C copy; a modest population-level association with adiposity.
comparisons.CC: Two C copies; generally a larger average association than CT, not a prediction of personal weight.

variants.dietMeaning: Use observed hunger, satiety and weight trends rather than a genotype-specific calorie formula.
variants.limitations: Common-region associations must not be equated with rare monogenic obesity.

variants.geneRole: FGF21 is a liver-derived hormone involved in nutrient signalling and food preference.
variants.variantMeaning: A common synonymous marker associated with the proportion of carbohydrate/sweet foods consumed in human studies.
variants.evidence: Human dietary-preference associations; causal mechanism and intervention utility remain uncertain.

comparisons.GG: No A copies at this marker; comparison group in several intake studies.
comparisons.AG: One A copy; associated with a tendency toward higher carbohydrate/sweet intake at population level.
comparisons.AA: Two A copies; does not prove cravings, high sugar intake or an FGF21 deficiency.

variants.dietMeaning: Use the person’s actual preferences and intake; do not infer that more sugar is needed or prescribe an FGF21-related treatment.
variants.limitations: A synonymous marker can tag a regulatory effect elsewhere. It is not a direct hormone-level test.

variants.geneRole: Encodes a mitochondrial enzyme that converts superoxide into hydrogen peroxide for further processing.
variants.variantMeaning: A protein change in the mitochondrial targeting sequence; forward A corresponds to Val and G to Ala at the commonly described position 16.
variants.evidence: Functional cell/protein evidence; clinical diet translation is uncertain.

comparisons.AA: Val/Val at this targeting-sequence marker. Not a direct oxidative-stress measurement.
comparisons.AG: Val/Ala. No reliable halfway antioxidant requirement is established.
comparisons.GG: Ala/Ala. Differences in mitochondrial import do not establish that this genotype is universally healthier.

variants.dietMeaning: Do not prescribe antioxidant megadoses from this call. Assess the overall diet and actual clinical context.
variants.limitations: Both reactive-oxygen production and clearance are complex; no personal oxidative-stress score or longevity estimate is inferred.

variants.geneRole: Helps transport and clear cholesterol-rich lipoprotein particles.
variants.variantMeaning: One of two markers contributing to the common apoE protein isoforms; T corresponds to Cys and C to Arg at the traditionally numbered position 112.
variants.evidence: Established protein/isoform biology; sensitive multi-marker interpretation is withheld.

comparisons.TT: Cys/Cys at this position. This alone cannot distinguish the complete common APOE types.
comparisons.CT: Cys/Arg at this position. A complete APOE type is not assigned from this single call.
comparisons.CC: Arg/Arg at this position. Bloom does not infer an APOE type or disease risk here.

variants.dietMeaning: Use measured lipids and cardiovascular context. Bloom does not select a diet or supplement from these individual APOE entries.
variants.limitations: No APOE haplotype, Alzheimer disease risk, combined type or diagnosis is inferred, even when both markers are present.

variants.geneRole: Helps transport and clear cholesterol-rich lipoprotein particles.
variants.variantMeaning: The second common isoform marker; C corresponds to Arg and T to Cys at the traditionally numbered position 158.
variants.evidence: Established protein/isoform biology; sensitive multi-marker interpretation is withheld.

comparisons.CC: Arg/Arg at this position. The other APOE marker and haplotype context are still relevant.
comparisons.CT: Arg/Cys at this position. Bloom does not assign a complete APOE type.
comparisons.TT: Cys/Cys at this position. This is not a diagnosis of a lipid disorder.

variants.dietMeaning: Use measured lipids and cardiovascular context. Bloom does not select a diet or supplement from these individual APOE entries.
variants.limitations: No APOE haplotype, Alzheimer disease risk, combined type or diagnosis is inferred, even when both markers are present.

variants.geneRole: Encodes GLUT2, a transporter involved in glucose movement and sensing.
variants.variantMeaning: The Thr110Ile protein variant has been associated with reported sugar intake; forward A corresponds to the Ile-associated allele.
variants.evidence: Small human dietary-association studies; no validated dietary prescription.

comparisons.GG: No A copies; Thr/Thr at the described protein change.
comparisons.AG: One A copy; carriers of the Ile allele reported higher sugar intake in the cited study.
comparisons.AA: Two A copies; the study’s grouped carrier results do not establish a precisely greater effect than AG.

variants.dietMeaning: Actual sugar intake and glucose measurements matter; this marker does not establish intolerance, a craving diagnosis or a personal sugar limit.
variants.limitations: Association with self-reported intake is different from a proven causal effect or a validated genotype-specific intervention.

variants.geneRole: Encodes apolipoprotein A-II, a component of HDL involved in lipid metabolism.
variants.variantMeaning: A promoter variant studied for interactions with saturated fat. Forward G corresponds to the gene-oriented -265C allele; forward A corresponds to -265T.
variants.evidence: Replicated observational gene–diet interaction; no individually validated threshold.

comparisons.AA: Gene-oriented TT: the non-CC comparison group in the cited studies.
comparisons.AG: Gene-oriented TC: generally grouped with TT in the cited recessive-model comparison, not assumed halfway to GG.
comparisons.GG: Gene-oriented CC: associated with higher BMI particularly at higher saturated-fat intakes in several cohorts.

variants.dietMeaning: Consider the overall fat pattern and measured lipids; do not turn a study intake cutoff into a personal prescription.
variants.limitations: The comparison is conditional on diet and study design, not a universal ranking of good and bad genotypes.

variants.geneRole: Participates in lipid handling in liver cells.
variants.variantMeaning: The G allele encodes the I148M change associated with increased liver-fat susceptibility.
variants.evidence: Strong human association and functional evidence; expression depends on other factors.

comparisons.CC: No G copies; comparison group for this marker, not proof of a healthy liver.
comparisons.CG: One G copy; increased average susceptibility compared with CC.
comparisons.GG: Two G copies; generally a stronger liver-fat association than CG, not a diagnosis or severity stage.

variants.dietMeaning: Use liver assessments and metabolic context; this SNP does not choose a supplement or prescribe an exact diet.
variants.limitations: Actual liver fat, inflammation and fibrosis cannot be determined from the genotype.

variants.geneRole: Contributes to export of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins from the liver.
variants.variantMeaning: The T allele encodes E167K and is associated with liver-fat and circulating-lipid differences.
variants.evidence: Replicated human association with functional support.

comparisons.CC: No T copies; comparison group at this marker.
comparisons.CT: One T copy; associated with more liver fat but often lower circulating lipid levels.
comparisons.TT: Two T copies; uncommon, so precision is more limited. Do not infer a personal effect size from copy count.

variants.dietMeaning: Interpret liver health and blood lipids separately; lower cholesterol does not establish less liver fat.
variants.limitations: No individual dietary response or diagnosis follows from this marker alone.

variants.geneRole: Regulates glucokinase activity and the handling of glucose in the liver.
variants.variantMeaning: The T allele encodes P446L and is associated with higher triglycerides but lower fasting glucose on average.
variants.evidence: Replicated human metabolic-trait association.

comparisons.CC: No T copies; comparison group in the cited analysis.
comparisons.CT: One T copy; population averages can shift toward higher triglycerides and lower fasting glucose.
comparisons.TT: Two T copies; generally a larger average trait shift, not an individually predicted concentration.

variants.dietMeaning: Review glucose and triglycerides together; a low glucose result alone does not describe all metabolic risk.
variants.limitations: This is not a genetic carbohydrate limit, insulin-resistance diagnosis or reason for a particular supplement.

variants.geneRole: Regulates whether lactase expression persists after childhood, affecting lactose digestion.
variants.variantMeaning: A marker in an MCM6 regulatory region influences the neighbouring LCT gene. Forward A corresponds to the commonly described persistence-associated -13910T allele.
variants.evidence: Established functional association in relevant ancestry groups; symptoms depend on more than this SNP.

comparisons.GG: Compatible with lactase non-persistence at this marker; does not diagnose lactose intolerance.
comparisons.AG: One persistence-associated A copy is generally sufficient for persistence; this is not necessarily halfway between GG and AA.
comparisons.AA: Two persistence-associated A copies; compatible with lactase persistence, not a guarantee that dairy causes no symptoms.

variants.dietMeaning: Use the amount of lactose actually tolerated; this marker alone does not require avoiding all dairy.
variants.limitations: Other lactase-persistence variants occur in different populations. Milk allergy, lactose intolerance and other digestive problems are different conditions.
